commits.summary: Example 307 ahead of the preservation stream's step 6: where the checker stops, the callee's footprint, the conversions on the pinned JDKs, and countermodels for the model and the rule
commits.body:
New files only, for the watcher of the domain-advances run to pass on as guidance within step 6; no claim, note, checker source or stream file is changed. examples/307-*/records/step-6-packet.md is the account. Six capped probes of the preservation stream's rmvpqswzxlyv (step-6-probes.json): 307's preservation stops in 1 s at the previous revision's getBytes("UTF-8"), the mutant's at StandardCharsets.US_ASCII, and with the conversions modelled the claim's unwind 513 leaves no loop summarized, so nothing is tied and the check is killed at 4 GB in 39 s; at the default unwinding it ends at the time limit as 287 does.

records/callee-footprint/footprint.py reads class files and says what a callee's closure reads, writes and hands on: hashpw(byte[],String) is the same 13 methods and initializer in before, after and the mutant, writes nothing its caller can see and reads five final tables nothing else writes (hashpw-bytes.json); 287's crypt_raw is the same in 6.3.7 and 6.3.8, whose hashpw differs by nine inserted instructions (287-crypt-raw.json). records/conversion/ runs both getBytes overloads, the US-ASCII conversion and written-out encoders on 4.3 thousand million Strings on Temurin 21.0.13 and 25.0.5 with no difference, and records the overloads' bytecode. records/mutant-witness.json says which candidates the real cipher tells apart.

lib/tests/fixtures/conversion-countermodels (twelve pairs, a prototype model as a patch, the test to add) and callee-countermodels (ten pairs for taking an unchanged callee as one function) each have a harness, check.py, and a README with what a JVM and today's checker say. Verified by running them: the prototype decides its six pairs, a prototype made wrong on purpose is caught on six, today's checker proves none of the seven callee countermodels and proves 307's shape in the miniature. validate_example.py 307 and the test-cost lint pass. Also found: the example route passes no --assume for an equivalence task, a witness a second run undoes is reported as not reproduced, and a parameter named b does not compile in the generated pair.

commits.summary: Example 307: a prototype of the relation at the unchanged callee closes both tasks at crypt_raw on JDK 25, and the callee's code has no fingerprint there at hashpw(byte[], String)
commits.body:
A second delivery from the session the user brought in ahead of the preservation stream's step 6, for the stream to compare its own call-level rule against. New files, and edits to this session's own fixture; no checker source and no test changes.

examples/307-*/records/step-6-call-level.md is the note and step-6-call-level-probes.json the runs. lib/tests/fixtures/callee-countermodels/prototype-one-function.patch (against kskmpmny, git 10b5d9c0, after prototype-model.patch) names a callee's outcome by the key of the state at its entry, as a loop's state past the bound is named, and checks no side condition. With it, at the claim's frozen parameters and assumption, in capped probes (4 GB, 300 s): with the relation at crypt_raw on JDK 25, preservation is verified in 79 s (878 MB) and the mutant is a violation in 58 s, replayed on a JVM; with it at hashpw(byte[], String), preservation is verified in 53 s on JDK 21 and the run is killed at 4 GB on JDK 25, and the mutant has no verdict under the claim's seven salts (the first candidate has salt = null) and is a violation under one valid salt. Without a relation the runs die at 4 GB.

The JDK 25 difference: hashpw(byte[], String) calls Integer.parseInt, whose bytecode the checker follows, and JDK 25's parseInt(String, int) calls String.format(String, Object[]), which shared::reach takes as a way back into the application since kskmpmny. The fixture gains the row parsed (Parsing.java, a callee that calls Integer.parseInt): verified on JDK 21 and no verdict on JDK 25 on kskmpmny, in under a second.

The prototype against the fixture's rows: by formula it falsely proves wiped and counted (what the callee writes is not in its outcome); with a relation by content added it falsely proves table, seeded, helped and aliased too. No other row turns. So the rows separate a rule with its side conditions from one without.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the code two versions are taken to share past the reach's fix: an override removed, a hidden field, an interface's initializer two ways and the target's own class's, each taken as identical or tied where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's kskmpmny (its fix for domain-advances-preservation-I010). The fix holds: built apart with the sources touched, tie_countermodels.rs passes there, its checker-side test included. Past it, lib/src/shared.rs's reach still leaves out five things, each shown by lib/tests/fixtures/reach-countermodels (old/ against new/), where each version alone gives 2 (0 for hidden) against 1 on a JVM (lib/tests/reach_countermodels.rs). Under the defaults, each of these is 'identical in both versions; nothing to prove' at kskmpmny and on this line alike, since the shortcut is older than the run: removed (an override the previous version declared and the new one inherits; only the new version's reach is walked and the old one is looked up by the new one's declaring class), hidden (a field the previous version declared that hides an inherited one; fields are not compared), constant (an interface's static read through an implementing class; the JVM initializes the interface, initialized() takes superclasses only), defaulted (making an object initializes a superinterface with a default method) and Own#f (the target's own class's initializer). looped, constant's read in a loop past the bound, is Verified under the ties at kskmpmny, non-vacuous; on this line it gets no verdict.

shared.rs is the preservation stream's this run, so nothing in lib/src changes here: the README's checker-side test, which fails on all six at kskmpmny, goes to it as a failure item citing this commit. Audit: the shortcut needs no --before-classpath, which 288 to 290 all pass; 289's rerun on kskmpmny unwinds fully; 287's BCrypt implements no interface and uses only its own fields in both pinned releases. No accepted result is affected. Inbox I004 is acknowledged as waiting: preservation's call-level rule is not committed yet. Verified: the changed tests under MemoryMax=8G with --rust-jobs 1 passed after test_costs.py estimate and tag; lint agrees.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a stand-in a lemma's proof rested on, and of an Error a logged record's getter raises with no athrow, each proved with nothing stated where a JVM says otherwise
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge brief, against state's stand-ins (qlylowvo, prove --stand-in) and preservation's logging fix (lqkwokqq). A lemma's proof is a check of its own, given the check's stand-ins. The check that uses the lemma states the lemma as proved, and states only what its own run's engine noted. So at state's zlvqxmst, built apart, sn.Use#viaLemma is Verified through a lemma whose proof called a narrowly sampled stand-in, and its result names no stand-in; a JVM gives 32 where 0 is proved (lib/tests/fixtures/stand-in-countermodels). A model on request is lost the same way. Preservation's scan refuses athrow in a logged record's classes, but a JVM raises an Error without one: an OutOfMemoryError (new long[Integer.MAX_VALUE]) and a StackOverflowError (a recursion) in getMessage() each leave log through StreamHandler.publish's catch (Exception). Both are Verified 'log returned' at kskmpmny (lib/tests/fixtures/log-countermodels). The rules are those streams', so nothing in lib/src changes; each README has the checker-side test, which goes to the owner as a failure item. No accepted result rests on either: 286's simpleMatch lemma calls only String methods, and 287's LocationResolvingLogRecord neither recurses nor allocates by input.
